## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money via to_money and round_money: Always convert incoming monetary values with to_money() and round them with round_money() from ledgerly/money.py before storing them on models; compare against ZERO from the same module rather than literal 0.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable error codes: Reject invalid input by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly/errors.py with the established codes: "invalid_state" for wrong invoice status, "invalid_quantity" for bad quantities, "negative_amount" for negative money.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool when validating ints: When validating an integer argument, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since True/False are ints in Python.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc before arithmetic: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `subscriptions.current_period`); never compare raw datetimes directly.
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
